headline: The Trump administration is leaning on existing liability law to police AI safety, but it is unclear who would pay when an AI system causes harm.
score_reason: Pool 7 kept: a fresh Bloomberg analysis of live White House policy and pending bills, but it analyses steps already announced and is not a new official action.
importance_line: People harmed by a rogue AI system and the businesses that use AI agents are affected first, then regulators and developers such as OpenAI and Anthropic, as the White House relies on lawsuits and existing law, but who would pay remains legally unsettled.
summary: Bloomberg reports that the Trump administration is relying on existing liability law rather than new rules to keep AI safe, and that its new Super Intelligence Force warned developers late on Friday 9 Oct 2026 that they must report and fix incidents involving their models. Legal experts told Bloomberg that current hacking and product-liability law may not clearly reach an AI agent (software that acts on its own), and that it is unsettled whether the developer or the business using the tool would be responsible.
